title: Ardic 2025 cannot support a component correspondence: the glyph is not located on an identified folio, and the phonetics are chosen per word by language filters
statement: I read the open PDF (Turk Kulturu 63/XVIII-2, 2025, pp. 71-108) rather than the step's summary, and located the two places that decide whether a component correspondence is testable. First, phonetic values are not fixed by the sign: for the p. 84 syllable-letter the paper prints several Latin equivalents under the heading 'Latin Alphabet Equivalent' and states that these represent the POSSIBLE sound values, tested through what it calls 'phonetic determination and reconstruction' linguistic filters, with only one value finally chosen so that the sign 'is represented by a single sound value everywhere it occurs' across 240 pages. That is a key fitted per word by meaning, not a deciphered sign, and it is the same failure mode as Newbold's recomposition (P-R-006): the rule that picks the value consults the sense of the result. Second, the p. 84 crop is not tied to any folio in the paper, and the claims that are tied to folios are given as solved pages rather than as a tested mapping: f33v is read in a separate symposium paper, the last page is read as the name METMET with the paper itself noting that 'a few words' remain undetermined and that a full translation of that page has not been made, and the SAZAK/sesame identifications are offered as support for a claim described as 'scientifically proven'. A component correspondence needs the opposite order: the mark located on a named folio, boundaries preregistered, then the mapping tested on marks not used to build it. On the positive side, and this is worth recording because it is checkable independently, the paper does state a structural observation about Turkish that the manuscript appears to share: words do not end in /b/, /c/, /d/ or /g/ and do not begin with /h/, /j/, /m/, /n/, /r/, /v/ or /z/. That is a plain distributional claim about two corpora and it can be measured without adopting the alphabet. The graphical parallelism the step screens (tughra strokes, Greek flourishes, charter initials all combining an upright with a long sweep) is real at the level of coarse features, but coarse features recur in every chancery hand of the period, which is why the step's own request for matched stroke count, aspect ratio and role is the right control and has not been done.
check: Two separable tasks, and only the second is cheap. (a) The component correspondence stays INCONCLUSIVE until the authors name the folio for the p. 84 glyph and fix one phonetic value per sign before testing: with several allowed values per sign and a linguistic filter choosing among them, no mask can be preregistered and no annotator agreement is meaningful. (b) The distributional claim IS testable now, on the manuscript alone, with no key: measure whether certain paragraph words end in the EVA glyphs proposed for /b/ /c/ /d/ /g/ and begin with those proposed for /h/ /j/ /m/ /n/ /r/ /v/ /z/, and compare the resulting exclusion rates with the same measurement on Old Turkish and on the pinned reference languages poured into the same layout. If the manuscript shows the same consonant exclusions as Old Turkish and the references do not, that is a fact about the manuscript that does not depend on the disputed alphabet at all, and it would be the strongest thing this direction has produced. If the exclusions are generic to the references too, the observation is not evidence of Turkish. Do (b) before any further tughra comparison.

evidence.source: Ahmet Ardic, 'Multisyllabic Structuring of Syllable-Letters in the ATA Manuscript and the Ottoman Tughra', Turk Kulturu 63, XVIII-2 (2025), 71-108, https://www.turkicresearch.com/files/articles/4072.pdf
evidence.phonetics_chosen_per_word: the p. 84 figure lists several Latin equivalents as possible sound values, resolved by 'phonetic determination and reconstruction' filters so that one value is used everywhere
evidence.folio_not_named: the p. 84 crop carries no folio identifier in the paper
evidence.last_page_incomplete: the paper states a few words on the final page remain undetermined and no full translation of that page has been made
evidence.self_description: the SAZAK identification is presented as support for a claim the paper calls 'scientifically proven'
evidence.checkable_distributional_claim: no word ends in /b/ /c/ /d/ /g/; no word begins with /h/ /j/ /m/ /n/ /r/ /v/ /z/
evidence.comparators_screened: Yale MS 408 f1r lowest paragraph opening; Vatican Barb. gr. 166 f239r (1476); Marseille charter of 10 March 1425, AD Bouches-du-Rhone B 641 p. 8
evidence.verdict: component correspondence INCONCLUSIVE pending a named folio and fixed values; the consonant-exclusion claim is testable now and should be done first
